subdomain: 3.3 Evaluate accuracy-latency trade-offs and justify configuration decisions

en.question: A service's answers already meet its accuracy requirement. Users see nothing until a complete answer arrives, and complain that the interface appears frozen. The team enables streaming while keeping the model, retrieval, and generated content unchanged. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: Streaming establishes that retrieval and tool execution now finish sooner.
options.note: Streaming changes when generated output is delivered, not the execution time of retrieval or external tools. Those stages require their own measurements.

options.text: The first visible token can serve as the completion timestamp for the answer-quality service level.
options.note: A first token is not a completed answer and cannot demonstrate that the final response meets quality requirements. Completion must be measured at the application's actual outcome boundary.

options.text: Streaming can improve perceived responsiveness, but total completion latency still needs measurement.
options.note: Delivering output before generation finishes can reduce the visible wait. It does not establish a reduction in time from the user request to a complete acceptable answer.

options.text: Streaming permits lowering the accuracy gate because users can inspect partial answers sooner.
options.note: Earlier visibility does not change the application's accuracy requirement. Partial content may still be revised, interrupted, or insufficient for the user's task.

references.title: Anthropic Engineering: Demystifying evals for AI agents
